title: Propeller pitch system, blade 1
description: The propeller pitch system as one graph -- its parts, the interfaces between them and the dimensions and gaps that join them -- whose joints are bound to 3D geometry for the linkage solver and through which every pitch study is a chain. Most of its bands are placeholders; none should be quoted as a tolerance.

provenance.variation_only: Scoped since the 2026-10-26 fold: every edge that came from pitch_system, and every edge a pitch_system study selects, has `nominal: 0.0`. What follows is that document's own statement, still true of those edges. EVERY dimension in this document has `nominal: 0.0`. These are not lengths -- they are tolerance bands about an unstated nominal, because that is what the source sheet holds: a column of total tolerance widths, not dimensions (its own row 72 comment: 'note this is total range (divide by 2 for +/-)'). So min/max are -w/2 and +w/2 for a stated total width w, and a study's `nominal` total is 0 by construction while its worst-case and RSS bands are the real result. Mixing a nominal-carrying dimension into this topology would make the nominal column read as a position sum when it is not one; if real nominal lengths arrive, they arrive for ALL of these edges at once, or in a separate topology. The fold put both kinds in one document, so the rule is now per study: a study folds variation-only terms or absolute ones, never a mix (tests/test_topology.py pins the seven pitch_system studies).
provenance.geometry_not_in_the_bands: Nominal geometry that IS known -- pitch arm radius 50 mm, blade root radius 32 mm, pitch link length 105.9908 mm at a 77 deg link angle, gas-spring bushing separation 34.7 mm -- is carried in `properties` on the edge or transform it belongs to, never in a `dimension`. It is context for a transform, not a term in a variation sum. Known is not the same as verified, and `properties` has no `confidence` field to say which: every figure in that list rests on a workbook alone, which the SOP makes `untraced`. joint.description: The 5-place joint in DETAIL B: NAS6403U11D bolt down through the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing) and a plain bushing, through a 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, retained by a slotted nut + cotter pin over a flat washer.
joint.scope: Grip length only, and only along the bolt axis. Out of scope, deliberately: diameter and hole fits; bushing-to-bore interference; the pitch link's own internal stack; the joint at the other end of the pitch link; torque and preload.

pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.title: Pitch link to pitch plate grip length
pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.scope_note: The nodes and the edge orientation are a READING of the stack's element order and roles, not a sourced claim, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json's structure note describes for the L1 proof. The stack's axial order from the bolt head, complete since 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit): bushing, pitch-link eye, flanged-bushing flange, pitch-plate lug, washer. Until that date the eye had no element to hang an interface on and the flange was not known to exist, so this topology omitted both and said so here; the stack modelling both (the eye as a loudly-marked placeholder) is what lets this graph carry them without inventing anything the stack does not claim. The bolt's own fastener dimensions (grip, overall length, cotter-hole-to-point) are read as edges sharing additional interfaces beyond the clamped stack's own (the bolt's point, and the cotter-hole centreline), which is what turns this graph into more than L1's single grounded loop: the clamped-stack/grip loop (closing at the derived `shank_out` gap) and the length/grip/thread-region loop (closing at the derived `thread_region` edge), which share the bolt-head interface.

joint.description: The rotor (hub-and-blade) balance-mass retention bolt: a single fastener, selected at assembly from a nine-member NAS6403 grip family, clamping an optional countersunk washer, zero or more stacked balancing masses, and a flat washer against whatever structure carries the tapped hole at this section.
joint.scope: Grip length only, along the bolt axis. Deliberately out of scope: which of up to 10 balance-hole locations is used and how the 200 g total balance budget is allocated; torque; the safety-cable capture; diameter and hole fits; thread-engagement depth into the tapped member.

rotor_fastener_length.title: Rotor balance-mass bolt grip length
rotor_fastener_length.scope_note: A reading of the stack's own element order and roles, not a sourced claim. The stack's own notes give the clamped order from the bolt head: MS21299C3 washer, [balancing mass(es) -- MISSING], NAS1149V0332H washer, [receiving-structure thickness -- MISSING], then whichever of the nine as-drawn NAS6403 grip options is installed. Neither missing member is modelled as a node or edge -- there is no element to hang one on. The nine grip options are modelled as parallel structural edges between shared interfaces (`head_bearing_face`/`shank_full_dia_end`), all naming a single part, `fastener_family` -- see that part's own note for why separate part ids per option were rejected. A study selecting more than one of the nine simultaneously is refused by `BranchAmbiguity` at both of those interfaces, which is the topology's own way of enforcing 'exactly one dash is ever installed', mechanically rather than only in prose.

vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.title: VPA output to pitch plate grip length
vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.scope_note: The nodes and the edge orientation are a READING of the stack's element order and roles, not a sourced claim. The stack transcribes workbook rows E63-E67 as an ordered clamped stack (bushing, spherical bearing, bushing flange, pitch flange, under-head washer) plus the fastener grip; laying those out head-side-first, as a chain of six clamped-stack faces, is this handoff's own arrangement. Two things make that safe to publish: a chain sum is invariant to the ordering (a signed term list does not care), and tests/test_topology.py pins the study's totals against the stack's own published check. What it is NOT is evidence that these specific faces mate in this order on the real part -- see notes.

notes: One model of the product since 2026-10-26: the pitch_system topology was folded into this one, and its seven studies are studies of this graph. The notes after this one were written for the two documents separately; each describes its own half as it was then, and a count in one is that document's. Studyless by design. This topology has no studies and is not an analysis. It is a map of the pitch linkage's joints built to be bound to 3D geometry in apps/annotate/, so that scripts/fit_bound_features.py can hand the `linkage` solver nominal joint locations in the assembly frame at 72 degrees. Summing anything here would be summing a document that deliberately holds almost no numbers.

The only edge that carries a value is `pitch_link_length`, derived from the 3DX sweep sheet's own two node columns and cited cell-for-cell -- and cited `untraced`, because the only support is that workbook. The derivation settles `traced` against `inferred`; it says nothing about whether a second document stands behind the number, and the SOP's rule is that workbook-only support is `untraced` and goes on the gap list however reasonable it looks. Every other edge carries no dimension at all. That is this repo's cite-or-gap rule applied honestly to a document whose numbers have not been acquired: an `untraced` band of 0.000 would put a plausible number on a reader's screen, and a reader cannot tell a placeholder zero from a measured one. Each valueless edge's own `note` says in one line what would close it -- a named drawing, or a fit of a named mesh.

A consequence worth knowing: the DAG page's gap list reports an edge whose dimension is *unverified*, not an edge that has no dimension at all (scripts/build_topology_projection.py, `topology_gaps`), because a valueless edge there has always meant 'the quantity a study computes'. So this document's gaps are visible on its edges, each rendered as a value with no source, and only `pitch_link_length` reaches the gap list -- as a value with no tolerance band recorded, which it is. Filed as ISSUE_20260930_a_valueless_structural_edge_is_invisible_to_the_gap_list.md.

What has a mesh today, which is what decides what Jeff can bind: the pitch-link bearing (`spherical_bearing_pitch_link`), the pitch plate (`pitch_plate_215177_001`), the gas spring (`gas_spring`), the gas-spring mount (`gas_spring_mount_213668_002`), the tangential link mount (`tan_link_mount_215175_002`), the whole tangential link (`tan_link_212956_005` and its two bearings), and -- since rotorkit's 2026-10-01 extraction -- the `hub` and the `pitch_arm`. Still without a row: `pitch_link`'s body and `blade_root`, whose meshes ARE installed but whose identity is open, because blade 1 carries the instrumented variants of both. The annotator's 'no installed mesh' empty state is the honest answer for those two until that is decided.

The two pitch-link joint centres are nodes of the link, not of the bearing, because they are two instances of one bearing part and a topology part id names a part. The bearing carries its own features instead -- its ball centre against its seat and against its bore -- and a `gap` edge from that ball centre to each of the link's two joint centres says which geometry a reader binds for each.
